name: Karen Pierce
life: “I still remember the last correctly addressed letter my cousin sent.” People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Karen by a small Wednesday habit. Karen checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I need his lunch hours to date a letter he sent me. The price of soup is my only clue.
appearance: Karen is easy to recognize by thick, tightly coiled hair and a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones. Usually dressed in a rust-colored canvas coat with a thin silver ring worn on a cord, Karen listens with the head tilted a little to the left when listening.
personality: Karen loves an audience until a private hurt enters the room. Then the performer disappears and someone very good at getting other people through a door takes over.
agenda: To date the letter from the price of lunch.
family: Allen Marin is Karen’s older relative by marriage. Karen sets the time to leave. Allen picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *A red mitten*, Allen says, “I knitted it left-handed. I can still make its mate if the owner remembers the stripes.”
connections: Carla Lam. A date on the old bill belongs in the lawyer's account of the unclaimed debt.

reactions.response: Karen asks who owns the personal information on the tab before any of it leaves the counter.

reactions.situation: A street musician can't finish a familiar song
reactions.response: Karen starts a quiet conversation with the most impatient onlookers so the musician can recover their own time.
